claim: API Gateway now lets you raise the integration timeout of Regional REST APIs and private REST APIs beyond the prior limit of 29 seconds, but this might require a reduction in your account-level throttle quota limit. Edge-optimized REST APIs keep an integration timeout of 50 milliseconds - 29 seconds, which cannot be increased.
question: Which REST API endpoint types can now raise the integration timeout above the old 29-second limit, and at what cost?

values.display: Regional REST APIs and private REST APIs

qualifiers.scope: Regional and private REST APIs; edge-optimized REST APIs unchanged
qualifiers.condition: Raising the timeout might require a reduction in the account-level throttle quota limit.

evidence.quote: Amazon API Gateway increased integration timeout limit — If you’re using Regional REST APIs and private REST APIs in Amazon API Gateway, now you can increase the integration timeout limit greater than 29 seconds.
You can raise the integration timeout to greater than 29 seconds for Regional REST APIs and private REST APIs, but this might require a reduction in your account-level throttle quota limit.
| Integration timeout for edge-optimized APIs | 50 milliseconds - 29 seconds for all integration types, including Lambda, Lambda proxy, HTTP, HTTP proxy, and AWS integrations. | No |
evidence.table_header: | Resource or operation | Default quota | Can be increased |

note: Current truth: api-gateway-rest-timeout-regional, -private and -edge. Older exam questions assume a hard 29-second limit.
